t: Sections 4540(c), 7212(a), and 9540(c) of title 10, United States Code, are each amended by striking out “1071–1153” and inserting in place thereof “305, 3324, 5101–5115, 5331–5338, 5341, 5342, and 7154”.

fable.w: This is a purely technical conforming amendment that replaces cross-references in title 10. It involves no outside party, consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue; nothing here crosses the federal boundary into a decision process.
fable.s: are each amended by striking out “1071–1153” and inserting in place thereof “305, 3324, 5101–5115, 5331–5338, 5341, 5342, and 7154”.

qwen_block.w: This section is a technical amendment to the United States Code, specifically updating cross-references to other statutory sections. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. It is purely legislative housekeeping.
qwen_block.s: Sections 4540(c), 7212(a), and 9540(c) of title 10, United States Code, are each amended by striking out “1071–1153” and inserting in place thereof “305, 3324, 5101–5115, 5331–5338, 5341, 5342, and 7154”.

opus.w: This is a technical amendment that replaces outdated cross-references in title 10 with updated section numbers. It does not mention any process that involves people outside the federal government. The changed references are not participation either, because the text sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory committee or right to sue.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** One could read the cross-references (for example, to 5 U.S.C. 3324 or 5101–5115) as bringing in personnel procedures that involve outside parties. That reading fails because the section only swaps one set of section numbers for another. It does not set up any consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body or right to sue, and nobody outside the federal government is involved in any decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a technical amendment that updates statutory cross-references within Title 10 of the U.S. Code. It does not create any new processes for consultation, public comment, or involvement by non-federal entities. It merely changes the section numbers cited in other laws, which is an internal legislative housekeeping matter.
qwen_chat.s: Sections 4540(c), 7212(a), and 9540(c) of title 10, United States Code, are each amended by striking out “1071–1153” and inserting in place thereof “305, 3324, 5101–5115, 5331–5338, 5341, 5342, and 7154”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might think that changing statutory references could implicitly change participation requirements if the referenced sections contained them. However, this section is purely a technical amendment updating cross-references to other parts of the U.S. Code. It does not itself establish any process for consultation, comment, or involvement by non-federal parties. It does not mention any outside entities, advisory boards, public hearings, or rights to sue. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
